# Standard Library Reference

Each page is generated from `std/<module>.cp`.
Prelude items need no `use` in programs; everything else uses `use std.<module>.{Name}`.

| Module | Prelude exports | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| [`std.algebra`](algebra.md) | `Action`, `Commutative`, `Desc`, `Each`, `Group`, +15 | Operations as values: what a range structure folds with.  A structure never asks "what is the sum of two `T`s"; it is handed the operation. Most of the time that is a bare operator: `SegTree<V, Int>(max, a)` and `SegTree<V, Int>(+, a)` are the same tree with two operations. An operation of your own is the pair `Monoid(id, op)`; a lazy update is an `Action`. `desc(x)` reverses an order inside a sort key or a heap entry, and a non-commutative value says how it reads backwards with `Reversible`. |
| [`std.bag`](bag.md) | `SortedBag`, `SortedMap`, `SortedSet` | Ordered multiset and set with order statistics, range views, and cursors: `SortedBag<K>`, `SortedSet<K>`. |
| [`std.beats`](beats.md) | `BeatsSegTree` | Segment Tree Beats (Ji Driver) for range chmin, chmax, add, sum, min, and max.  Maintains exact `min`, second `min`, `max`, second `max`, and `sum` on every node. Range `chmin`, `chmax`, `add`, and `sum`/`min`/`max` queries run in \(O(\log n)\) amortized (\(O(\log^2 n)\) amortized when mixing `chmin`/`chmax` with `add`). |
| [`std.bitset`](bitset.md) | `Bitset` | A dense set of positions of a domain, 64 per word. |
| [`std.deque`](deque.md) | `Deque` | Double-ended queue: `Deque<T>`. |
| [`std.derive`](derive.md) | `Hash` | The `Eq`, `Ord`, `Show` and `Hash` a struct gets field by field, as library code on `fields` (decision 28.7), for an `impl` to call: `impl Ord for Job: fn lt(a, b) = lt_fields(b, a)` orders the other way, and `impl Hash for P: fn hash(self) = hash_fields(self)` is a struct's whole `Hash`. Each costs \(O(\mathit{fields})\) plus what its fields' own operations cost. |
| [`std.dp`](dp.md) | `LiChao`, `Line`, `LineContainer`, `MonotoneHull`, `aliens` | The DP toolkit: the structures and optimizations a DP calls by name.  A minimum or maximum of lines (the convex hull trick) is a `LiChao`; a layer whose optimal split moves right is `dnc_layer` (over `monotone_minima`); an interval DP with monotone splits is `knuth`; "exactly `k` pieces" over a convex cost is `aliens`. Meet in the middle starts from `subset_sums`; sums over subsets and supersets of masks are `std.ntt`'s `sos(mut f, over: Sub \| Sup = Sub, inverse:)`. The recurrence itself stays in your code, and a memoized recursion is `@memo`. Each optimization names the law it needs; `std.spec` checks it on small inputs (`monge_break`, `dnc_break`, `knuth_break`, `convexity_break`). A sliding-window optimum is `a.windows(k).fold(op)` or `std.window.Window(op)`. |
| [`std.dsu`](dsu.md) | `Dsu`, `DsuOf`, `ParityDsu`, `PotentialDsu` | Disjoint sets over a domain, with optional values per set, parities, and rollback. |
| [`std.fenwick`](fenwick.md) | `Fenwick`, `Fenwick2D` | Fenwick tree (binary indexed tree) over a domain: point add, range sum. |
| [`std.flow`](flow.md) | `Arc`, `FlowGraph`, `max_closure` | Flows, cuts and matchings: Dinic's max flow and min cut, min-cost flow, maximum closure, bipartite and general matching (weighted too), assignment, bounded flows, Gomory-Hu and global min cut.  Two networks, `FlowGraph` and `CostFlow`, share `Arc` and the accessors `flow`, `cap`, `source`, `target`. Everything whose input is a table or an edge list is a function over the caller's domains: a matching is `[L]?R`, a bounded flow is `[E]Int`. |
| [`std.geometry`](geometry.md) | `ByAngle`, `Location`, `Pt`, `locate`, `turn` | Plane and 3D geometry on exact integer points (`Pt`, `Pt3`) and careful floating-point vectors (`Vec`). Exact predicates compute cross and dot signs in `I128` so integer geometry is the default overflow-free path:  - `\|x\|, \|y\| <= 1e9` (e.g. `Pt<-1e9..=1e9>`): differences in `[-2e9, 2e9]`; single-vector `dot`/`cross` <= `2e18` fit `Int`, `turn`/`cross128`/`dot128` <= `8e18` fit `I128` with 19 orders of magnitude to spare, and `any_segments_meet` sweep comparisons <= `1.6e28` fit `I128`. - `\|x\|, \|y\| <= 2e18`: `turn`/`cross128`/`dot128`/`dist2_128` <= `8e36` fit `I128`. - 3D `\|x\|, \|y\|, \|z\| <= 1e9`: `cross3` components <= `8e18` fit `Int` (or `I128` up to `1e12`), and `convex_hull_3d` orientation tests <= `4.8e28` fit `I128`. |
| [`std.graph`](graph.md) | `Functional`, `Graph`, `Lit`, `Target`, `Tree`, +12 | Graphs: one stored representation and the algorithms over "what comes after v".  Vertices and edges are domains, so per-vertex data is `[V]T`, per-edge data is `[E]T`, and mixing the two does not type-check. An algorithm takes any `Next<V>`: a stored `Graph`, a `[V]List` of arcs, or any fn from a vertex to a `Seq` of arcs. An arc is anything with `.to`; what else it carries (`.w`, `.e`) decides which algorithms accept it:  bfs(g, from: [s]) dijkstra(g, from: [(s, 0)])                          # arcs carry w dijkstra(g.weighted(a => 2 * a.w), from: [(s, 0)])   # weights from a fn bfs(p => p.adj4.filter(q => grid[q] != '#'), from: [start]) bridges(g)                                           # arcs carry e  Customizing a graph is a lambda over `g.out(u)`; nothing is rebuilt. Unreachable is `None`. Whole-graph algorithms need `V: Domain`. |
| [`std.grid`](grid.md) | `Dir4`, `Dir8`, `adj4`, `adj8`, `ray`, +1 | Grids: a cell is the pair `(Row, Col)` and there is no grid type. `[Row, Col]T` is the grid, and this module adds what a cell can do: `p.up` (and `down`, `left`, `right`), `p.adj4`, `p.adj8`, `p.step(d)` and `p.ray(d)`. A grid is a graph by writing its moves: `bfs(p => p.adj4.filter(q => g[q] != '#'), from: [s])`. |
| [`std.hashmap`](hashmap.md) | `Counter` | Open-addressing hash map for `Int` keys with splitmix64 salting.  `FlatMap<V>` stores keys, values, and occupancy states in flat parallel arrays with linear probing and power-of-two capacity, avoiding per-node heap allocations when built-in `HashMap<Int, V>` overhead matters. |
| [`std.heap`](heap.md) | `Heap`, `MaxHeap`, `MinHeap`, `Settle` | Binary heaps (round 5): `Heap<T>(by:)` pops the smallest key first and `Heap(by: desc)` the largest. One type per shape: `Heap`, `ErasableHeap`, `IndexedHeap`, `MeldHeap`, `MinMaxHeap`.  Ties: no heap here is stable. Among elements with equal keys under `by:`, which one `peek` shows and `pop` returns is unspecified (but `peek` always shows the one `pop` returns next). Without `by:`, equal elements are indistinguishable, so this never shows. For a fixed order among equals, put the tie-breaker in the entry: `(d, v)`, or `(d, desc(v))`. |
| [`std.interval`](interval.md) | `IntervalMap` | Interval partition map (ODT / Chtholly tree): `IntervalMap<D, T>`. |
| [`std.io`](io.md) | `Wire`, `io`, `read_all`, `yes` | Answer words for yes/no problems. `print`, `read` and the `io` context are core (spec/core/10-io.md); this module holds the library half. |
| [`std.lazy`](lazy.md) | `Flip` | Range-update helpers that are not segment trees: `Flip`, `LazyTreap`, `Rope`. Range apply on a segment tree is `SegTree(op, a, act:)` (`segtree.cp`). |
| [`std.marks`](marks.md) | `Marks` | Opt-in generation-stamped mark table: `add`, `in`, `remove`, and `clear` are all \(O(1)\).  For sparse resets prefer `[D]Bool` with a touched list; import `std.marks.Marks<D>` when repeated full clears inside a loop would otherwise cost \(O(T \cdot N)\). Each `clear()` bumps a 32-bit generation counter instead of touching the underlying array, resetting the table only if the counter reaches its 32-bit ceiling. |
| [`std.math`](math.md) | `BigInt`, `Ratio`, `Sieve`, `Sign`, `bit`, +16 | Number theory on plain `Int`s. |
| [`std.matrix`](matrix.md) | `Mat` | Dense matrices, exact and floating-point Gaussian elimination, and GF(2) XOR bases.  `Mat<T>` stores an `rows x cols` matrix in flat row-major order (`data[r * cols + c]`). Exact elimination (`det`, `rank`, `solve`, `solve_space`, `inverse`) works over any field type with `T.zero`, `T.one`, exact `==`, and `/` (such as `Mod<P>` for prime `P`). Floating-point elimination uses partial pivoting with an explicit tolerance `eps` via `det_real`, `rank_real`, `solve_real`, and `inverse_real`. |
| [`std.mo`](mo.md) | *(import)* | Mo's algorithm: offline ordering and window stepping over `Range<D>`. |
| [`std.mod`](mod.md) | `Comb`, `Mod` | Modular arithmetic and counting.  `Mod<P>` is a number modulo a constant `P`: the modulus is part of the type, takes no memory, and two moduli cannot be mixed by accident. The modulus may be a constant (`type Z = Mod<998244353>`) or a value read from the input (`let p: Int = read()`, then `type Z = Mod(p)`): one type serves both. `P` may be anything below 2^62 (so `a + b` fits): above 3.03e9, where `P * P` no longer fits an `Int`, `*` multiplies in 128 bits. |
| [`std.ntt`](ntt.md) | `Curved`, `convolve` | Number-theoretic transform, exact and modular convolution, SOS, and bitwise transforms.  Polynomials are coefficient lists, lowest degree first (`p[k]` is the coefficient of `x^k`). There is one `convolve`: `on:` says how indices combine and `over:` which semiring the values live in; the value type picks the algorithm (NTT for an NTT-prime `Mod<P>`, three primes and CRT for any other `Mod` or `Int`, FFT for `F64`), and `cpl explain` names it. `cyclic: Bool = false`: - linear (`cyclic: false`): length `a.len + b.len - 1` (or `[]` if either input is empty) - cyclic (`cyclic: true`): requires `a.len == b.len`, length `n = a.len`, index `(i + j) % n`. |
| [`std.opt`](opt.md) | `and_then`, `is_none_or`, `is_some_and` | Methods of optionals (`?T`, core 2.4). The operators (`??`, `!`, `if let`, `match`) are core; these are ordinary fns over them. |
| [`std.pair`](pair.md) | `Pair` | Unordered pairs of distinct positions: the domain of data given once per pair. |
| [`std.persistent`](persistent.md) | *(import)* | Persistent segment tree and static range k-th smallest queries.  Each update copies only the \(O(\log n)\) nodes on the root-to-leaf path and returns a new `Version` handle. All earlier versions remain readable in \(O(\log n)\). |
| [`std.poly`](poly.md) | `eval` | Formal power series operations over NTT-friendly `Mod<P>`.  Series are plain `List<Mod<P>>` (lowest degree first: `a[k]` is `[x^k] a(x)`), matching `std.ntt.convolve`. Every truncated operation takes an explicit output length `n >= 0` (computing modulo `x^n`, returning length `n`; `n == 0` returns `[]`). |
| [`std.prefix`](prefix.md) | `Diff`, `Prefix`, `scan` | Prefix sums, prefix/suffix monoid folds, and offline difference arrays.  Call `Prefix(a)` on a `[D]T`, `[R, C]T`, or `List<T>` to build static prefix sums in \(O(n)\) or \(O(r \cdot c)\), then answer any `.fold(...)` or `.prefix(...)` query in \(O(1)\). Use `Diff<D, T>()` or `Diff<R, C, T>()` for \(O(1)\) offline range/rectangle adds and \(O(n)\) / \(O(r \cdot c)\) `finish()`. |
| [`std.rand`](rand.md) | *(import)* | Random numbers from a seed: the same seed gives the same numbers in `cpl run` and in the built C++. `Rng(seed)` is a splitmix64 stream: \(O(1)\) per draw. |
| [`std.search`](search.md) | `bsearch_real`, `split_best`, `ternary_max`, `ternary_max_real`, `ternary_min`, +1 | Search on answers: binary, exponential, ternary and parallel searches, and fractional programming. Each returns a position of the space searched or `None`, never a sentinel, and names the monotone or unimodal law it needs. Binary search over a range is a method on it (`std.seq`): `r.first_true(ok)`, `r.last_true(ok)`, `r.bsearch(ok, last:)`. Sorted lookup in a container is the four-name family `first_ge`/`first_gt`/`last_le`/`last_lt`; a search inside a range structure is its `right_while`/`left_while`. |
| [`std.segtree`](segtree.md) | `SegTree` | Segment tree over a domain, for any associative operation. |
| [`std.seq`](seq.md) | `Anchor`, `Compressed`, `Perm`, `RingSlice`, `Slice`, +48 | Sequences: reductions, scans, runs, searching, permutations, monotone stacks, and compression.  - Reductions & extrema: `prod`, `is_sorted`, `min`/`max` (with `by:`), `argmax`/`argmin` (with `by:`). - Binary & unimodal search: moved to `std.search` (`bsearch_real`, `ternary_max`/`ternary_min`, `ternary_max_real`/`ternary_min_real`, `parallel_bsearch`). - Sorted lookup: `first_ge`/`first_gt`/`last_le`/`last_lt` (with optional `by:`), returning `?D` on `[D]T`, `?Int` on `List<T>`, and `?(K, V)` on `Map<K, V>`. - Runs, chunking & windows: `runs`, `run_ranges`, `chunk_by`, `buckets`, `windows`, `chunks`, `pairs`, `with_prev`, `cyclic_pairs`, `zip`. - Scans & folds: `scan`, `suffix_scan`, `excl_fold` (cut-indexed `prefix_fold`/`suffix_fold` live in `std.prefix`). - Reordering & selection: `reverse`, `rotate_left`/`rotate_right`, `dedup`/`deduped`, `partition`, `select`, `merge_sorted`. - Permutations: `next_permutation`, `prev_permutation`, `inverse`, `compose`, `perm_cycles`, `perm_pow`, `inversions`. - Monotone stack & sliding extrema: `prev_less`, `next_less`, `prev_greater`, `next_greater`, `sliding_min`, `sliding_max`. - Coordinate compression: `let (domain C, xs) = compress(all)` -> `Compressed<C, T>` (`at`, `try_at`, `contains`, `first_ge`, `first_gt`, `last_le`, `last_lt`). |
| [`std.slope`](slope.md) | *(import)* | Integer-indexed concave and convex functions as sorted slopes (slope trick).  `Concave` keeps `f` on `lo..=hi` as `f(lo)` plus the multiset of slopes `f(c + 1) - f(c)`, largest first, in a lazy treap; `Convex` is its mirror. |
| [`std.sparse`](sparse.md) | `SparseTable` | Sparse table: \(O(1)\) range folds of a fixed array. |
| [`std.spec`](spec.md) | *(import)* | Checking observations on small cases: is a table monotone, convex, unimodal or Monge, does a cost satisfy the quadrangle inequality or a split table Knuth's bound, and which recurrence does a sequence follow. Each checker returns the first witness that breaks the law (`None` when it holds), so a brute force over small inputs can print it; the recurrence tools then extend a pinned sequence to any index. |
| [`std.strings`](strings.md) | `Palindromes`, `RollingHash`, `SuffixArray`, `common_prefix_len`, `common_suffix_len`, +13 | String algorithms. They only compare elements, so they work on a `Str` (ASCII bytes) and on any `List<T>` alike. Positions are 0-based. |
| [`std.subset`](subset.md) | `Subset` | Subsets of a small domain as one machine word: the mask of mask DP with its domain kept. |
| [`std.timetree`](timetree.md) | *(import)* | Offline segment tree over time (divide-and-conquer on life intervals).  Turn any rollback-capable data structure (e.g. `Dsu` with `.mark()` / `.undo_to(snap)`) into a dynamic structure with insertions and deletions over `[0, q)` in \(O(q \log q)\) apply/undo steps. |
| [`std.tree`](tree.md) | `JumpTree`, `KruskalTree`, `LcaTable`, `Lift`, `PreferredPaths`, +2 | Rooted trees: parents, subtree ranges, LCA, and path folds over one range structure.  Each `Rooted` tree value `t` owns a fresh domain, `t.Pre`: the positions of an Euler order in which every subtree and every heavy chain is one contiguous range. `t.pos(v)` is a `t.Pre`, not a `V` (and never mixes with another tree `t2.Pre`), so indexing a per-position structure with a vertex or another tree's position does not type-check.  `Rooted` is the one tree abstraction. A value per vertex lives in any structure indexed by `t.Pre` (a `SegTree`, with or without `act:`, a `Fenwick`), and `fold_path` / `apply_path` walk a path over it, so there is no second "tree with values" type and no second copy of the data. |
| [`std.window`](window.md) | `Sweep`, `Track`, `Undo`, `Undoing`, `Window`, +2 | Sliding-window folds and stateful windows (round 7, `lib/sequence-patterns.md`).  `a.windows(k).fold(op)` and `Window(op)` pick their strategy from the op's laws: a `Group` adds and subtracts, a `Selective` op keeps a monotone deque, anything else uses two stacks. State that is not a fold implements `Track` (`push`/`pop`); two pointers, Mo and divide-and-conquer DP all accept a `Track`. |
